fieldMarks: Huge ground bird, 1.1-1.2 m long, with a naked head and a long, wide tail.
Trimmer and stronger-looking than the domestic barnyard turkey.
Females and young are smaller and duller than adult males.
behavior: Males gobble in spring and strut with feathers puffed, tail fanned, wattles swollen and wings drooped; one male mates with several females.
Usually walks or runs but flies strongly; roosts overnight in tall trees.
Forages on the ground, scratching leaf litter, most actively in early morning and evening; acorns are a favourite food.
Not migratory, but may wander, especially in fall.
habitat: Varies across the continent: oak-hickory and pine-oak forests, cypress swamps, mesquite grassland, pinyon-juniper and chaparral, usually near oaks. Best habitat mixes woodland and open clearings.
range: Native to North America; depleted by 1900 but reintroduced to most of its former range and established in new areas, now found across the United States and in southern Western and Eastern Canada, and adapting to suburban edges in the East.
